request: why is momentum conserved when two carts collide?

beats.intent: A 2 kg cart moving right at 3 m/s towards a 1 kg cart at rest
beats.narration: A two kilogram cart rolls right at three metres per second towards a one kilogram cart at rest.
beats.code:
stage.title("Conservation of momentum")
track = draw_line(stage, (-6, -1.2), (6, -1.2))
a = Rectangle(width=1.4, height=0.8, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.8).move_to([-4, -0.8, 0])
b = Rectangle(width=0.9, height=0.6, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.8).move_to([0.5, -0.9, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(a), FadeIn(b))
stage.add(a, b)
va = Arrow(a.get_top() + UP * 0.2, a.get_top() + UP * 0.2 + RIGHT * 1.5, buff=0, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(GrowArrow(va))
stage.add(va)
stage.label(a, "2 kg, 3 m/s", direction=DOWN + DOWN)

beats.intent: The carts colliding and sticking, moving on together at 2 m/s
beats.narration: They collide and stick together, moving on at two metres per second.
beats.code:
stage.play(VGroup(a, va).animate.shift(RIGHT * 3.35), run_time=1.2)
stage.remove(va)
both = VGroup(a, b)
stage.play(both.animate.shift(RIGHT * 2.5), run_time=1.5)
vb = Arrow(both.get_top() + UP * 0.2, both.get_top() + UP * 0.2 + RIGHT * 1.0, buff=0, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(GrowArrow(vb))
stage.add(vb)

beats.intent: Bars of momentum before (6) and after (6) beside 2×3 = 3×2
beats.narration: Momentum before is two times three, six; after it is three times two, six. It is conserved.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
bars = draw_bars(stage, [6, 6], labels=["before", "after"])
stage.equation(r"2 \times 3 = (2 + 1) \times 2 = 6")

request: do heavy things fall faster than light ones?

beats.intent: A heavy ball and a light ball side by side at the same height
beats.narration: Drop a heavy ball and a light ball from the same height, ignoring air.
beats.code:
stage.title("Falling together")
heavy = Dot([-1.5, 2.5, 0], radius=0.35, color=GREY_B)
light = Dot([1.5, 2.5, 0], radius=0.15, color=YELLOW)
ground = draw_line(stage, (-4, -2.5), (4, -2.5))
stage.play(FadeIn(heavy), FadeIn(light))
stage.add(heavy, light)

beats.intent: Both balls falling and hitting the ground at the same moment
beats.narration: They speed up at the same rate and land together.
beats.code: stage.play(heavy.animate.move_to([-1.5, -2.15, 0]), light.animate.move_to([1.5, -2.35, 0]), run_time=1.5, rate_func=rate_functions.ease_in_quad)

beats.intent: Axes with one curve d = 5t^2 shared by both
beats.narration: Both follow the same law: distance fallen is five t squared, whatever the mass.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 3), y_range=(0, 45), labels=("s", "m"))
g = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda t: 5 * t ** 2, color=YELLOW, label="d = 5t^2")
stage.caption("Same curve for any mass")

request: how do you work out the work done pushing a box?

beats.intent: A box on the floor with a force arrow of 20 N pushing it
beats.narration: Push a box with a steady force of twenty newtons.
beats.code:
stage.title("Work = force × distance")
floor = draw_line(stage, (-6, -1), (6, -1))
box = Square(side_length=1, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.8).move_to([-4, -0.5, 0])
push = Arrow(box.get_left() + LEFT * 1.2, box.get_left(), buff=0, color=RED)
stage.play(FadeIn(box), GrowArrow(push))
stage.add(box, push)
stage.label(push, "20 N", direction=UP, color=RED)

beats.intent: The box sliding 5 m to the right
beats.narration: It slides five metres.
beats.code:
stage.play(VGroup(box, push).animate.shift(RIGHT * 5), run_time=2)
br = Brace(Line([-4, -1, 0], [1, -1, 0]), DOWN)
stage.play(GrowFromCenter(br))
stage.add(br)
stage.label(br, "5 m", direction=DOWN)

beats.intent: Axes of distance against force with a 20 N by 5 m rectangle shaded, beside W = 100 J
beats.narration: On a force-distance graph the work is the area: twenty times five, a hundred joules.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
ax = draw_axes(stage, x_range=(0, 6), y_range=(0, 25), labels=("m", "N"))
line = plot_graph(stage, ax, lambda x: 20, x_range=(0, 5), color=RED)
shade_area(stage, ax, line, 0, 5)
stage.equation(r"W = 20 \times 5 = 100\ \text{J}")

request: why does a sharp knife cut better than a blunt one?

beats.intent: Two blades pressing down with the same 50 N force, one thin edge and one wide edge
beats.narration: Press two blades down with the same fifty newtons: one sharp, one blunt.
beats.code:
stage.title("Pressure = force / area")
sharp = Polygon([-3.5, 1, 0], [-2.5, 1, 0], [-3, -1, 0], color=GREY_B, fill_opacity=0.8)
blunt = Polygon([1.8, 1, 0], [4.2, 1, 0], [3.8, -1, 0], [2.2, -1, 0], color=GREY_B, fill_opacity=0.8)
stage.play(FadeIn(sharp), FadeIn(blunt))
stage.add(sharp, blunt)
for x in (-3, 3):
    a = Arrow([x, 2.3, 0], [x, 1.1, 0], buff=0, color=RED)
    stage.play(GrowArrow(a), run_time=0.4)
    stage.add(a)

beats.intent: The contact edges lit: a tiny one under the sharp blade, a wide one under the blunt
beats.narration: The sharp blade touches a tiny area; the blunt one spreads the force over much more.
beats.code:
e1 = Line([-3.05, -1, 0], [-2.95, -1, 0], color=YELLOW, stroke_width=10)
e2 = Line([2.2, -1, 0], [3.8, -1, 0], color=YELLOW, stroke_width=10)
stage.play(Create(e1), Create(e2))
stage.add(e1, e2)

beats.intent: Bars of the pressure under each: sharp far taller than blunt
beats.narration: Pressure is force over area, so the tiny edge gives a huge pressure that cuts.
beats.code:
stage.clear()
bars = draw_bars(stage, [50 / 0.1, 50 / 1.6], labels=["sharp", "blunt"])
stage.equation(r"p = \frac{F}{A}")

request: why does oil float on water?

beats.intent: A glass with a layer of oil on top of water
beats.narration: Pour oil into water and it floats on top.
beats.code:
stage.title("Why oil floats")
glass = Rectangle(width=2.5, height=4, color=WHITE).shift(LEFT * 3)
water = Rectangle(width=2.5, height=2.5, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.6).align_to(glass, DOWN).set_x(glass.get_x())
oil = Rectangle(width=2.5, height=1, color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=0.6).next_to(water, UP, buff=0)
stage.play(Create(glass), FadeIn(water), FadeIn(oil))
stage.add(glass, water, oil)
stage.label(oil, "oil", direction=RIGHT, color=YELLOW)
stage.label(water, "water", direction=RIGHT, color=BLUE)

beats.intent: Bars of density: oil 0.9 and water 1.0 g/cm³
beats.narration: A cubic centimetre of oil weighs about point nine grams; the same amount of water weighs one gram.
beats.code: bars = draw_bars(stage, [0.9, 1.0], labels=["oil", "water"], where="right")

beats.intent: The glass beside the rule: less dense liquids rise to the top
beats.narration: The less dense liquid ends up on top.
beats.code: stage.caption("Less dense floats on more dense")

request: how far away is a cliff if the echo comes back after 2 seconds?

beats.intent: A person on the left and a cliff wall on the right with a sound pulse leaving
beats.narration: Shout towards a cliff. The sound travels out at three hundred and forty metres per second.
beats.code:
stage.title("Timing an echo")
you = Dot([-5, -1, 0], radius=0.2, color=YELLOW)
cliff = Rectangle(width=0.6, height=4, color=GREY, fill_opacity=0.8).move_to([5, 0, 0])
stage.play(FadeIn(you), FadeIn(cliff))
stage.add(you, cliff)
pulse = Arc(radius=0.5, angle=PI / 2, start_angle=-PI / 4, color=BLUE).move_to([-4.3, -1, 0])
stage.play(pulse.animate.move_to([4.4, -1, 0]), run_time=1.5)

beats.intent: The pulse bouncing back to the person
beats.narration: It bounces off the cliff and comes back. The round trip took two seconds.
beats.code:
stage.play(Rotate(pulse, PI), run_time=0.2)
stage.play(pulse.animate.move_to([-4.3, -1, 0]), run_time=1.5)
br = Brace(Line([-5, -2, 0], [4.7, -2, 0]), DOWN)
stage.play(GrowFromCenter(br))
stage.add(br)
stage.label(br, "d", direction=DOWN)

beats.intent: The scene beside 2d = 340 × 2, d = 340 m
beats.narration: The sound went there and back, twice the distance: so the cliff is three hundred and forty metres away.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"2d = 340 \times 2 \Rightarrow d = 340\ \text{m}")

request: where is the balance point of a rod with two weights?

beats.intent: A rod from 0 to 6 with a 2 kg weight at 0 and a 4 kg weight at 6
beats.narration: A light rod six metres long: two kilograms at one end, four at the other.
beats.code:
stage.title("Centre of mass")
nl = draw_number_line(stage, x_range=(0, 6))
w1 = Square(side_length=0.6, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.8).next_to(nl.n2p(0), UP, buff=0)
w2 = Square(side_length=0.85, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.8).next_to(nl.n2p(6), UP, buff=0)
stage.play(FadeIn(w1), FadeIn(w2))
stage.add(w1, w2)
stage.label(w1, "2 kg", direction=UP, color=BLUE)
stage.label(w2, "4 kg", direction=UP, color=RED)

beats.intent: A pivot triangle placed under x = 4
beats.narration: The balance point is nearer the heavier end: at four metres.
beats.code:
piv = Triangle(color=YELLOW, fill_opacity=1).scale(0.25).next_to(nl.n2p(4), DOWN, buff=0.05)
stage.play(FadeIn(piv))
stage.add(piv)

beats.intent: The rod beside x = (2·0 + 4·6) / 6 = 4
beats.narration: Weight times position, added, divided by the total weight: twenty four over six, four.
beats.code: stage.equation(r"\bar x = \frac{2 \cdot 0 + 4 \cdot 6}{2 + 4} = 4")
